name: Orange juice / vitamin C diet
lead: The orange juice or vitamin C diet refers to consuming large amounts of citrus juice or vitamin C, in the belief that it improves skin. Vitamin C is a cofactor in collagen synthesis, and this role is the basis for the appearance claims [2].

No published trial has tested mega-dose orange juice for skin. Wikipedia describes the health value of orange juice as debatable because of its high sugar content [1], and reference authorities set an upper intake level for vitamin C because large doses cause gastrointestinal effects [2].

paras: A 250 mL cup of orange juice has about 112 calories and 21 g of sugar, and is a rich source of vitamin C [1]. The US recommended dietary allowance is 90 mg/day for men and 75 mg/day for women [2].
Vitamin C is needed for enzymes that hydroxylate proline and lysine in collagen, and deficiency causes scurvy [2].
No studies found on orange-juice-centred diets for skin appearance.

The US Institute of Medicine set a 2,000 mg/day upper level in 2000 based on gastrointestinal effects above 3,000 mg/day. Large doses may also cause headache, sleep trouble and flushing [2]. Orange juice is acidic and sugar-rich, and some government guidance favours whole fruit and limiting juice [1].

lore.intro: Online, high-dose citrus and vitamin C are promoted for brighter skin.

claims.claim: Mega-dose vitamin C or orange juice improves skin quality.
claims.believers: Proponents cite vitamin C's role in collagen synthesis [2].
claims.experts: Reference bodies set upper limits, and no studies of juice-based protocols for skin are listed here [2].

card.summary: Heavy orange juice or vitamin C intake for skin, resting on vitamin C's collagen role; untested for appearance and sugar-heavy.
card.note: High doses cause GI effects; juice is high in sugar.

quick.overview:
This practice involves taking in large amounts of orange juice or vitamin C for skin. The idea rests on vitamin C's role in collagen formation.

No studies have tested it for appearance, and orange juice is high in sugar.
quick.mechanism: Vitamin C is a cofactor for collagen-building enzymes; whether extra intake beyond adequacy changes skin is untested in this context.
quick.risks: Doses above about 3,000 mg/day have caused diarrhea and other gastrointestinal effects, and the US upper level is 2,000 mg/day.
